definition: The rule that when waves overlap, the total field at each point is the sum of the individual fields.
Where a wave is in its cycle (crest, trough, or in between) at a given place and time; a half-wavelength shift puts crest against trough.
Overlapping waves arriving in step (crest on crest), so their amplitudes add and the spot is bright.
Overlapping waves arriving half a cycle out of step (crest on trough), so they cancel and the spot is dark.
The extra distance one wave travels compared with another to reach the same point; whole wavelengths give bright spots, odd half-wavelengths give dark ones.
Describes waves that keep a fixed phase relationship with each other, which is needed for a stable interference pattern (lasers are highly coherent).
Every point on a wavefront acts as a source of small wavelets; the next wavefront is the sum of those wavelets. It explains diffraction.
The spreading of a wave as it passes through an opening or around an edge, by an angle of roughly wavelength divided by opening width.
A surface with many evenly spaced slits or grooves that sends each wavelength off at its own angle, d sin(theta) = m lambda, splitting light into a spectrum.
The whole number m in d sin(theta) = m lambda that counts how many wavelengths of path difference produce a given bright fringe.
Interference between light reflected from the front and back surfaces of a very thin layer, which produces the colors of soap bubbles and oil slicks.
The wavelength of a moving particle, lambda = h/p; it makes electrons, neutrons, and even molecules diffract.
The quantum wave that travels through an apparatus (for example, both slits); its intensity at a spot gives the chance of detecting the particle there.
The small blurred disk with faint rings that a perfect circular lens makes from a single point of light, because of diffraction at the lens.
Two points are just resolved when their angular separation is about 1.22 lambda/D, so one's Airy peak falls on the other's first dark ring.
The smallest detail a lens-based instrument can resolve, set by wavelength: about lambda/(2 NA) for a microscope, or roughly half a wavelength at best.
A measure of how wide a cone of light a microscope objective collects; the best oil-immersion objectives reach about 1.4 to 1.5.
Weak scattering by objects much smaller than the wavelength, with cross-section proportional to d^6/lambda^4; it makes the sky blue.
Strong, complicated scattering by objects about the same size as the wavelength, such as haze, smoke, and milk droplets in visible light.
An antenna about half a wavelength long that is resonant and radiates efficiently (radiation resistance near 73 ohms).
